text: For finite n, S is generated by n independent, mutually commuting Hermitian involutive n-qubit Pauli operators and contains no minus identity. In the formal reconstruction, the 2^n subgroup cardinality is derived from these premises rather than assumed as a field.
G is a finite group, V is a complex vector space, rho is a linear representation of G on V, and the group cardinality is invertible in the scalar field.

A stabilizer code has an Abelian Pauli subgroup S and code space T equal to the common +1 fixed space of S. For an n-qubit code encoding k qubits, S has 2^(n-k) elements and T has dimension 2^k, provided the forbidden scalar phases are absent.
The source states that an n-generator stabilizer has only one joint +1 eigenvector.
For a stabilizer group S, the source uses the unnormalized operator sum over S and proves by left-multiplication reindexing that its output is fixed by every element of S.
For a finite linear group representation over the complex numbers, the normalized group-average map is a projection whose range is exactly the common fixed subspace.

quantifiers: linear representation rho of G on V
logical_form.conclusion: range(averageMap rho)=invariants(rho), and averageMap rho is idempotent

text: For finite n, a phase-normalized rank-n stabilizer S has a one-dimensional common +1 eigenspace. Any normalized vector spanning it is unique up to global phase, and its rank-one projector is the associated pure n-qubit stabilizer state.

logical_form.conclusion: dim Fix_+(S)=1 and the normalized ray defines a pure stabilizer state
